_doc: credit-verify-outbound.sh CAPACITY caps (Fable 10-30 23:4xZ: the fixed small daily caps go; the safety is the auto-kill: bounce / spam / unsub > 2 %, any fraud hit, the zero-read, v1's 2 h sample). daily_cap = users messaged per campaign per UTC day by segment (credit: the runner's own segment record; claim: ledger rows of the campaign). shared_daily_cap = every campaign of the group together per UTC day (m2's shared send cap inside notify: credit 2,500 / claim 500; messaging-monitoring-m2, H-DevOps #4598). A campaign with no row or no group never applies (fail closed). Raising a cap is a PR. holds = the Gmail-side DATED WINDOWS [key=dated-windows-are-data] (l1 ruling 2026-11-02, ruling-o-retire-1102.md): a code literal with a date in it is a CI red with a countdown on it. holds.gmail is the /o promise clause (an extra sentence in a uvn-status ask) and the hold on gmail-vouched users: clause_open=false retires it, due_at closes it on the clock. The gate re-reads this file on every run, so closing needs no deploy.

tick_cap._doc: Per-family per-tick cap. A family+segment listed here may ACCEPT at most this many users in ONE tick, whatever its daily row, its FIRST_CAP line or the global CVO_CAP says. The clamp only ever LOWERS a cap - a value above the family's own cap changes nothing, so this key can never widen a blast radius. Absent family/segment = exactly the behavior before this key existed. Added 2026-11-04 on the Fable driver's ruling: the free uvn-status apply sends until its Intercom-note step hits the subprocess timeout at ~55-60 min / ~80 users and then loses its outcomes artefact entirely (#1756, twice in one afternoon: 39 sends at 15:05Z, 79 at 17:24Z). A per-FAMILY cap was needed rather than CVO_CAP because that knob is ONE global value: setting it to 60 would also have narrowed r1, claim-status and the approved 70-send claim install.
